title: Find lengths using similar triangles
show: two similar triangles ABC and PQR with matching sides AB=8, PQ=14, AC=12 marked

example.question: Triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$ are similar. $|AB| = 8$ cm and $|PQ| = 14$ cm are matching sides. $|AC| = 12$ cm. Find $|PR|$, the side that matches $[AC]$.

steps.say: Divide a side of the bigger triangle by the matching side of the smaller one. This gives $\hl{1}{k}$, the number that turns $ABC$ into $PQR$.
$PR$ matches $AC$. Multiply $|AC|$ by the scale factor $\hl{1}{k}$.
$PQR$ is the bigger triangle, so $|PR|$ should be bigger than $|AC| = 12$. It is.

rows.aside: Always check that the bigger triangle gets the bigger answer.

issues: Proportions contradict the question: |AC| = 12 is longer than |AB| = 8, but in triangle ABC the side AC is drawn shorter than AB (about 95 vs 102). Likewise |PR| = 21 should be longer than |PQ| = 14, but PR is drawn shorter than PQ (about 163 vs 181).
Given lengths 8, 14 and 12 cm are not marked on the figure.

title: Find the centre and scale factor of an enlargement
show: triangle ABC and its image PQR with lines through corresponding vertices meeting at the centre of enlargement

example.question:
The triangle $PQR$ is the image of the triangle $ABC$ under an enlargement.
(a) Construct the centre of enlargement and label it $O$.
(b) Given $|AB| = 4$ cm and $|PQ| = 10$ cm, find the scale factor $k$.
(c) Check your answer: $|OA| = 6$ cm. Find $|OP|$.

steps.say: Join each point to its image. The lines meet at one point. That point is the **centre** $O$.

rows.aside: Join $C$ to $R$ as a check. All three lines meet at $O$.

steps.say: The scale factor is image length over object length. $|PQ|$ is the image of $|AB|$.
Distances from $O$ scale by the same $\hl{1}{k}$. Multiply $|OA|$ by $\hl{1}{k}$ to get $|OP|$.

rows.aside: On the diagram you can measure $|OP|$ to confirm. Allow 5 mm either way.

issues: A, B, P and Q all lie on one line through O, so the lines A-P and B-Q coincide and do not meet at a point; the centre cannot be found by construction from this figure.
Scale is wrong: |AB| is about 20px and |PQ| about 65px (ratio about 3.2, not 2.5); |OP|/|OA| is about 3.4, not 2.5.
Labels A and B sit on the dotted lines and crowd each other; the figure is tiny.

title: Apply Corollary 6: Circles sharing a tangent at a point: the centres and that point are collinear
show: two circles touching externally at T with centres A and B and the line AB passing through T, radii marked

example.question: Two circles touch externally at $T$. Their centres are $A$ and $B$. The radius of one circle is $4$ cm and the radius of the other is $9$ cm. Find $|AB|$.

steps.say: Draw the tangent to both circles at $T$. A radius meets a tangent at a right angle.

rows.aside: $[AT]$ and $[BT]$ are both perpendicular to this tangent at $T$.

steps.say: Both radii are perpendicular to the same line at the same point. So $A$, $T$ and $B$ lie on one straight line. This is **Corollary 6**.

rows.aside: For external touching, $T$ is between $A$ and $B$.

steps.say: Along the line, $\hl{1}{|AB|}$ is made of the two radii.

rows.aside: If the circles touched internally you would subtract: $9 - 4 = 5$.

issues: Radii are not in proportion with 4 cm and 9 cm: the left circle has radius about 75px and the right about 57px (ratio about 1.3, should be about 2.25).
Radii and lengths 4 and 9 are not marked, though the figure is meant to show them.
Label T sits on the dashed line AB.

title: Apply Corollary 5: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°
show: cyclic quadrilateral ABCD with opposite angles A and C marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. $|\angle A| = (2x + 10)°$ and $|\angle C| = (3x - 20)°$. Find $x$.

steps.say: $A$ and $C$ are opposite corners of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

rows.aside: So Corollary 5 applies: opposite angles sum to $180°$.

steps.say: Add the two angles and set the total equal to $180$.
Add $10$ to both sides, then divide by $5$ to find $\hl{1}{x}$.

rows.aside: Check: $|\angle A| = 86°$ and $|\angle C| = 94°$. They add to $180°$.

issues: The quadrilateral is an isosceles trapezoid with the longer side DC at the bottom, so angle A is about 95 degrees (obtuse) and angle C about 85 degrees; the working says |angle A| = 86 and |angle C| = 94, the opposite way round.
Angles A and C are not marked on the figure.
